subtitle: Out Manila · Air China
overview: Spend four days in Beijing, then fly to Zhangjiajie for the “Avatar” scenery of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, the Grand Canyon glass bridge and the Xibu folk culture street. You fly Air China round trip from Manila and stay in local 5-star hotels. Several shop visits are included in the rate.
travelDatesNote: Departures from Manila, Feb 16–23 2027 to Feb 23–Mar 2 2027. The rate changes by date: an amount on a date is added to the base rate per pax. Seats are limited and confirmed at booking.

itinerary.title: Manila – Beijing
items: Fly Manila to Beijing (CA180, 06:20–10:50) and arrive at Beijing airport
Transfer to hotel and check in (lunch included)

itinerary.title: Beijing – Zhangjiajie
items: Meet your guide at Zhangjiajie airport, transfer to hotel and check in

itinerary.title: Zhangjiajie – Avatar scenic area
items: Avatar scenic area, up and down by Bailong Lift or Tianzishan cable car
After dinner, transfer back to hotel

itinerary.title: Zhangjiajie
items: Grand Canyon C Line – Glass Bridge
Xibu, the largest folk culture walking street
After dinner, transfer back to hotel

itinerary.title: Zhangjiajie – Beijing
items: Tianmen Mountain with cable car, glass skywalk and Tianmen Cave (optional)
Transfer to the airport and fly Zhangjiajie to Beijing (CA8610, 17:50–20:30)

itinerary.title: Beijing – Manila
items: Free and easy until transfer to the airport

placeDesc.Water Cube: The National Aquatics Center built for the 2008 Beijing Olympics, seen from outside.
placeDesc.Bird’s Nest: Beijing's National Stadium with its steel lattice design, built for the 2008 Olympics and seen from outside.
placeDesc.Wangfujing Walking Street: A busy pedestrian shopping and snack street in central Beijing.
placeDesc.Tiananmen Square: One of the largest public squares in the world, at the heart of Beijing.
placeDesc.Forbidden City: The vast former imperial palace of China's emperors, in the centre of Beijing.
placeDesc.Juyongguan Great Wall: A well-preserved section of the Great Wall at a mountain pass north of Beijing.
placeDesc.Summer Palace: A former imperial garden of lakes, bridges and pavilions on the edge of Beijing.
placeDesc.Temple of Heaven: A historic complex of temples and gardens where emperors held prayers for good harvests (optional tour).
placeDesc.Zhangjiajie Avatar scenic area: Sandstone pillar peaks in Hunan that inspired the floating mountains in the film Avatar.
placeDesc.Bailong Lift: A tall outdoor glass elevator built against a cliff, used to reach the Avatar scenic area.
placeDesc.Tianzishan Cable Car: A cable car that carries guests up to the Tianzi Mountain area with views over the sandstone peaks.
placeDesc.No. 1 Bridge: A natural stone bridge in the Zhangjiajie park, a scenic viewing stop in the Avatar area.
placeDesc.Avatar Hallelujah Mountain: The pillar mountain in Zhangjiajie that inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains in the film Avatar.
placeDesc.Grand Canyon Glass Bridge: A glass-floored bridge across a canyon near Zhangjiajie, walked on the Grand Canyon C Line.
placeDesc.Golden Whip Stream: A scenic stream valley in Zhangjiajie, walked between rock walls and forest.
placeDesc.Tujia Cultural Park: A park showing the culture and traditions of the Tujia people of the Zhangjiajie region.
placeDesc.Tianmen Mountain: A mountain near Zhangjiajie reached by cable car, with a glass skywalk and the Tianmen Cave (optional tour).
